approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would let the government charge levies on companies that build and run offshore electricity projects.
The Offshore Infrastructure Registrar and Regulator would collect the levies to cover costs not paid by fees under the main bill.
The levy details, such as amounts and how they are calculated, would be set out in regulations made later.
Imposes levies on regulated entities for offshore electricity activities.
Recovers costs for regulating the offshore electricity industry that fees do not cover.
Aligns cost recovery with the existing offshore petroleum and greenhouse gas storage regime.
Companies that carry out offshore electricity infrastructure projects, including transmission and generation, in the Commonwealth offshore area.

The Offshore Electricity Infrastructure (Regulatory Levies) Bill 2021 was introduced to ensure full cost recovery for the Offshore Infrastructure Registrar and Regulator, with NOPTA and NOPSEMA appointed to administer and regulate the framework, supporting the development of offshore electricity projects.

The speaker supported the Offshore Electricity Infrastructure (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2021, which establishes a regulatory framework for offshore wind projects in Commonwealth waters. They noted a proposed 600-megawatt wind project off Kingston, South Australia, in their electorate of Barker, and urged the proponent Australis Energy to engage the local community and ensure the project falls under Commonwealth rather than state jurisdiction.

The member for Bass supported the Offshore Electricity Infrastructure Bill 2021 and related bills, arguing they will create jobs, lower emissions, and attract investment in offshore wind and renewable energy. The member noted the Bass Strait has strong offshore wind potential and that the bills establish a regulatory framework for offshore electricity projects.
